title: Research with Evidence
summary: Plan, execute, verify, and recover a bounded AI-assisted research workflow.
objectives: Turn a research need into bounded questions and evidence requirements.
Use AI to organize sources without treating generation as a source.
Verify claim-to-source mappings and report disagreement or missing evidence.
Recover from weak searches, inaccessible sources, and unsupported synthesis.

sections.title: Prepare the question and evidence plan
paragraphs: State the decision the research supports, the questions that must be answered, the allowed time period, and the evidence strong enough for each claim. Separate facts, comparisons, estimates, and judgment.
Choose permitted data before searching. Do not upload confidential, personal, licensed, or organization-restricted material to a tool unless policy and authorization allow it.

code.label: Research brief
code.code:
Decision: [WHAT THIS RESEARCH SUPPORTS]
Questions: [BOUNDED QUESTIONS]
Scope: [TIME, REGION, PRODUCT, AUDIENCE]
Evidence required: [PRIMARY SOURCES, TESTS, DATA]
Allowed data: [CLASSIFICATION AND PERMISSION]
Stop conditions: [ENOUGH EVIDENCE OR ESCALATION]

sections.title: Execute with a source ledger
paragraphs: Search for primary sources, record canonical links and review dates, and note what each source can and cannot support. Use AI to extract candidate claims, organize themes, or identify gaps while keeping the original sources available.
Label generated suggestions as leads until verified. A model response, search snippet, or citation-shaped string is not evidence by itself.

sections.title: Verify every material claim
paragraphs: Open each cited source and compare the exact claim with the supporting passage, table, test, or record. Check publication scope, version, date, and whether the source is authoritative for the claim.
For consequential conclusions, seek independent evidence or review. Report disagreements and uncertainty instead of averaging incompatible claims into false certainty.

sections.title: Recover from evidence failure
paragraphs: If a source is unavailable, stale, circular, or unsupported, mark the affected claim and search for a stronger source. Narrow the question when the evidence cannot support the original scope.
When the evidence remains insufficient, deliver a gap report: what is known, what is disputed, what is missing, and the next safe action.

sections.title: Protect data and preserve provenance
paragraphs: Minimize copied data, redact unnecessary identifiers, and preserve license and attribution requirements. Store source metadata separately from generated prose so a reviewer can reconstruct the reasoning.
Before sharing, check that citations resolve, sensitive information is absent, and the conclusion does not exceed the evidence.
sections.callout: A trustworthy synthesis is reproducible from its source ledger.

activity.title: Produce a one-page evidence-led research brief
instructions: Choose a current, low-risk question and define its decision, scope, evidence requirements, allowed data, and stop conditions.
Build a ledger with at least three primary sources, supported claims, limitations, and review dates.
Draft a synthesis that maps each material claim to the ledger and labels uncertainty or disagreement.
Remove one source, identify what no longer holds, and write the recovery action.
evidence: A research brief, source ledger, and one-page synthesis with claim-to-source mappings.
A gap-and-recovery note showing the effect of the removed source.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Which conclusion changed most when you tested whether its source actually supported its scope?

cues.text: Build a research brief from decision, bounded questions, evidence, allowed data, and stop conditions.
Show questions flowing into a source ledger and then into supported claims.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: A text flow reads: decision, bounded questions, evidence requirements, source ledger, supported claims. Reduced-motion mode shows the entire flow.

cues.text: Separate AI-generated research leads from opened and qualified primary sources.
Ask learners to mark one candidate claim as verified, disputed, or unsupported.
Allow two minutes to complete one source-ledger row.
Demonstrate opening a source and checking passage, scope, version, date, and authority.
Turn a failed citation into a narrower claim, stronger search, or explicit evidence gap.
Review data minimization, attribution, provenance, and a final sensitive-data check.
Check that the learner can reconstruct one claim from the source ledger.
Guide the learner through the brief, ledger, synthesis, and removed-source recovery test.
Begin the check after every material claim is supported, disputed, or visibly marked as a gap.

questions.prompt: What should be defined before an AI-assisted search begins?
choices: The decision, bounded questions, scope, evidence requirements, allowed data, and stop conditions
questions.explanation: A bounded brief makes the research goal, evidence, safety, and completion conditions reviewable.

questions.prompt: How should an AI-generated source suggestion be treated?
questions.explanation: The original authoritative source must be opened and qualified before the suggestion becomes evidence.

questions.prompt: Two authoritative sources disagree within the task's scope. What is the strongest response?
choices: Report the disagreement, scope, and evidence and seek resolution or review
questions.explanation: Visible disagreement preserves evidence and avoids manufactured certainty.

questions.prompt: What should a synthesis do when evidence cannot support the requested scope?
choices: Narrow the claim or deliver an explicit gap report
questions.explanation: A narrower supported claim or gap report is more trustworthy than unsupported completion.

questions.prompt: What makes a research synthesis reproducible?
choices: A source ledger that maps claims to qualified evidence and records limitations
questions.explanation: The ledger lets another reviewer reconstruct and challenge the synthesis.
